newsitem.title: LUXEMBOURG: States may not prohibit imports of recovered meat - court.
newsitem.headline: States may not prohibit imports of recovered meat - court.

text.p: The European Court of Justice said on Tuesday member states may not prohibit imports of mechanically recovered meat, even if it is not heat treated before importation.

In a dispute between a meat importer and the local German health inspection authority, questions were raised about the application of Community rules governing the import of mechanically recovered meat from Belgium into Germany.

Mechanically recovered meat is defined as fresh meat taken from the bone in the form of pulp, obtained by mincing and sebsequent extraction from bones by pressing. This meat is highly perishable and unless heat treated is unfit for human consumption, according to court documents.
The German authority wanted the meat to be heated before importation, or at least to have its own veterinarian designate the establishment within Germany to carry out the heating process.
The court rejected Germany's arguments on the basis of Council directives 64/443, 91/497, and 89/608 and held the meat may be heated in either the exporting or importing state.
The exporting state may involve the importing veterinarian authorities without giving up the authority to designate the heat-treating establishment, the court said.
Reference from the Oberverwaltungsgericht fur das Land Nordrhein-Westfalen, Munster (Germany)
Paul Daut GmbH & Co KG and Oberkreisdirektor des Kreises Gutersloh
on the interpretation of Council directive 64/433/EEC on Community trade in fresh meat, directive 89/608/EEC on veterinary mutual assistance, and articles 30 and 36 of the EC treaty

1. Article 6(1)(c) and (g) of Council directive 64/433/EEC on Community trade in fresh meat precludes national rules that prohibit the import of mechanically recovered meat which has not been subjected to heat treatment in the member state of origin but is intended to be subjected to such treatment in an approved establishment in the member state of importation designated by the official veterinarian in the state of origin.

2. The competent veterinary authority of the member state of origin may, under Council directive 89/608/EEC, seek the assistance of the competetent veterinary authority of the member state of importation, without such a request affecting the right of the official veterinarian in the state of origin to designate an establishment for heat treatment in the member state of importation.
